justification: Changes when the fidelity gate declares an extracted regulatory number GROUNDED against its source PDF -- the check that decides whether a provision reaches a human as trustworthy or suspect. A wrong loosening here ships a false 'this is correct' signal on a planning control. Measured cause: the gate scoped number-checking to a single anchor page, so any clause straddling a page break was wrongly flagged. Of 433 flagged rows in the live queue, 428 were that false alarm and 5 were real errors -- a 1.2% true-positive rate that made the human queue unworkable, so it went unreviewed for days and the gate delivered no safety at all.

pre_impl.existing_data: The `pages` dict already fetched by gate_chapter via vf._page_text_for_chapter, and the row's own new_text. No new query, no new table, no new column, no additional R2 fetch.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The prior assumption was that a provision's numbers live on the page _best_page anchors to. False for real DCPs: clauses routinely continue across a page break, which _number_window's own docstring already predicted as an accepted residual. This corrects the assumption without widening the window that the masking guard depends on.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future gate run for every council. Does NOT retroactively re-grade rows already graded; the current queue was cleared separately by direct source verification.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The source is the council's own PDF text layer, already fetched. If that text layer is garbled (a real condition for map-heavy chapters), a genuinely-present number can still fail to match and the row stays flagged -- the safe direction. The change never turns a garbled-source read into a GROUNDED verdict on its own; the context requirement must also be met.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- no API or component change in this PR.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If this rescue were too loose, a fabricated control value would be marked grounded and reach a reviewer labelled 'matched to source', which is the exact false-confidence this gate exists to prevent. Guarded by requiring the number to carry >=60% of its own surrounding content words within a 260-character span of the candidate match, and pinned by a masking test using two unrelated 9.9 values.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The rescue stops recovering a genuine page-straddle (false alarms return), OR it starts grounding a number the chapter never states (the Gordon/Roseville case), OR it reinstates masking by letting an unrelated identical value ground a different clause.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Verified in BOTH directions against real production strings, not fixtures. RESCUE: ku_ring_gai's 'Create a consistent 3 storey (11.5 metres) street wall' grounds against the St Ives chapter text, whose PDF contains that exact phrase 3 times -- previously flagged. STILL FLAGS: the same rule against the Gordon chapter returns False, because the Gordon PDF (700,091 chars) contains neither '11.5' nor 'consistent 3 storey' -- confirmed by full-document search, and the same for Roseville (445,931 chars). That is a genuine cross-precinct copy error and the only real defect among 433 flagged rows; it must keep failing. NO MASKING: an unrelated '9.9 square metres in area' does not ground a '9.9 metres building height' rule. PROSE STRADDLE: '24 hour activity' grounds when the sentence continues on the next page. 46/46 pass in tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate.py; full suite 5,812 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.

functions.name: _straddle_grounded
functions.input: num (the number ruled absent from the narrow anchor-page window), text (the row's cleaned provision text), whole_chapter (all page texts joined -- already built in ground_row).
functions.output: bool. True only when the number is found somewhere in the chapter with at least _CONTEXT_MATCH (0.6) of the up-to-6 content words either side of it in the rule appearing within 260 characters of that occurrence. True removes the number from `absent`, so the row can grade grounded.
functions.if_none: Empty or missing num, text or whole_chapter returns False -- i.e. it never rescues on absent input, so a missing source leaves the row flagged rather than silently grounded. Covered by test_empty_and_missing_inputs_are_safe.

functions.name: looksLikeAControl
functions.input: num (a number the fidelity gate could not match) and the row's new_text, both arriving as untyped API JSON.
functions.output: bool -- true when a unit (m/mm/m2/%/storeys/metres/hectares) follows the number within 14 characters, i.e. it could be a real planning control rather than a figure number, page footer or ordinary prose. Drives a red CHECK THIS ONE banner versus a grey probably-nothing-to-fix banner.
functions.if_none: Non-string or empty input returns false, so an unreadable row shows the grey banner rather than throwing and blanking the review panel.

values.name: _CONTEXT_WORDS / _CONTEXT_MATCH
values.value: 6 words either side; 60% of them must appear within 260 chars of the candidate match
values.why: Chosen so the ku_ring_gai 11.5 case separates correctly in both directions on real data: St Ives rescues, Gordon and Roseville do not. Not independently calibrated across a wide sample -- see break_it.
values.source: Measured against the live dcp_review_queue and the councils' own R2-hosted PDFs, 2026-09-09.
values.if_missing: If the constants were absent or zero the rescue would never fire and every page-straddling clause would stay flagged -- i.e. exactly the pre-fix behaviour that produced 428 false alarms out of 433. There is no silent-wrong mode: _straddle_grounded returns False on any empty input, so a missing value degrades to the old, over-flagging behaviour rather than to over-grounding.
values.read_at: scripts/dcp_fidelity_gate.py -- _CONTEXT_WORDS and _CONTEXT_MATCH are module-level constants read only inside _straddle_grounded, which ground_row calls when filtering the absent-number list. No other module imports them.

break_it.scenario: The thresholds (6 context words, 60% match, 260-char span) were tuned against one real failure class -- the ku_ring_gai 11.5 cross-precinct copy -- not calibrated across a broad labelled sample. A different shape of fabrication could clear 60% by coincidence.
break_it.what_happens: A fabricated number that happens to sit near similar words elsewhere in the same chapter would be rescued and graded grounded, presenting a wrong control to a reviewer as source-matched.
break_it.how: Not fully mitigated. Bounded by three things: the match must be in the SAME chapter (not the corpus), the context words come from vf._content_words (>=4 letters, so 'the/and/of' cannot pad the score), and a real fabrication typically carries no shared context at all -- which is exactly why the Gordon case scores 0 rather than marginally. A broader calibration set would need labelled true/false examples that do not exist yet.
break_it.repro: tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate.py::TestStraddleRescue::test_does_not_reinstate_the_masking_bug pins the known masking shape; a novel one is unpinned by construction.

break_it.scenario: This changes only how rows are graded from now on. The 433 rows already in the queue were resolved separately by direct whole-document source verification (45 approved, 5 rejected as the real error), not by this code path.
break_it.what_happens: No back-fill: previously-graded rows keep whatever verdict they were given.
break_it.how: Deliberate -- re-grading historical rows would rewrite review decisions a human and an evidence-backed verification already made. Future runs get the corrected behaviour.
break_it.repro: SELECT fidelity_status, count(*) FROM dcp_review_queue GROUP BY 1 -- historical verdicts unchanged by this PR.

break_it.scenario: A chapter whose PDF text layer is badly garbled (map-heavy ku_ring_gai and city_of_sydney chapters are measurably like this) can fail the context match even when the number IS genuinely on the page, because the surrounding words are scrambled.
break_it.what_happens: The row stays flagged -- a false alarm survives.
break_it.how: Accepted, and it is the safe direction: the failure mode is 'a human looks at a correct row', not 'a wrong number ships as verified'. It also cannot be fixed here -- it is the OCR/text-layer problem tracked separately (DQ-97/DQ-98), not a grading problem.
break_it.repro: Any ku_ring_gai section-b map chapter: the extracted PDF text contains runs like 'B n A d C s K ca S ping 40%'.

break_it.scenario: The rescue scans every occurrence of the number in the chapter against every occurrence in the rule, so a very common short number (e.g. '2') in a long chapter multiplies the inner scan.
break_it.what_happens: Grading takes measurably longer on large chapters, since each already-absent number is scanned against every one of its own occurrences in the chapter text. It stays correct, just slower, and a slow gate delays the review queue rather than corrupting it.
break_it.how: Not optimised. Bounded in practice because it only runs for numbers ALREADY ruled absent by the narrow window -- a small subset -- and each inner check is a substring scan of a 520-char span, not a re-parse. Grading remains far cheaper than the PDF fetch that precedes it.
break_it.repro: N/A -- performance note, not a correctness defect.

break_it.scenario: The rescue only searches the SAME chapter. A number correctly stated in a DIFFERENT chapter of the same DCP (councils cross-reference between parts) will not be rescued.
break_it.what_happens: A legitimate cross-chapter reference stays flagged as a false alarm.
break_it.how: Deliberate and load-bearing: chapter scope is what made the Gordon/Roseville error detectable at all. Widening to the whole DCP would have rescued that fabricated 11.5 from the St Ives chapter and hidden the only genuine defect found in 433 rows. Cross-chapter false alarms are the price of catching cross-chapter fabrication, and they fail in the safe direction.
break_it.repro: tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate.py::TestStraddleRescue::test_still_flags_a_value_the_chapter_never_states -- that test only passes because the scope is per-chapter.

break_it.scenario: looksLikeAControl only inspects the 14 characters after the number. A control whose unit is separated by intervening words (for example 'a setback of 6, measured in metres') reads as noise and receives the grey banner.
break_it.what_happens: A genuine control is presented to the reviewer as probably-nothing, so it gets less attention than it deserves. The row is still shown in full with the source PDF beside it, so this de-prioritises rather than hides it.
break_it.how: Not mitigated. The 14-character window was chosen because every unit in the measured queue sat immediately after its number (1.8m, 600mm, 11.5 metres, 50%). Widening it pulls in the NEXT sentence's unit and marks ordinary prose as controls, destroying the triage the banner exists to provide -- 50 rows needing eyes would become hundreds again.
break_it.repro: frontend-nextjs/__tests__/components/dcp-review-number-context.test.ts::looksLikeAControl covers the measured shapes; a separated-unit phrasing is unpinned by construction.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- after the next scheduled dcp-extract --review run, check that the flagged count is a small fraction of what it was: SELECT fidelity_status, count(*) FROM dcp_review_queue WHERE status='pending' GROUP BY 1. A return to hundreds of flagged rows would mean the rescue is not firing.
